subject: Request: discretionary low-latency SLA for Luminate key account
messages:
From: James Park <james.park@luminate.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SLA uplift for Luminate enterprise product

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Luminate is preparing a commercial commitment for our core Realtime API (customer-facing embeddings + chat) and our CTO asked whether Redwood can commit to a tighter P95 for a small set of mission-critical calls. High level ask: 50ms P95 for inference on the public API for an identified subset of traffic (approx 2M calls/day at peak windows).

Key constraints from our side:
- This is a customer-critical flow (real-time chat in finance product).
- We can route a percentage of traffic to the low-latency path via our feature flags.
- We need clear runbook, escalation path, and a fallback policy (if you can’t meet the 50ms, we must have a graceful fallback variant).

Attaching our proposed scope and sample traffic profile — please let me know if this is something Redwood can consider as a discretionary SLA carveout. Important: Luminate expects a contractual SLA and a small service credit if not met.

Thanks,
James Park
Director, Platform Engineering — Luminate

Quick product note — thanks for looping me in. A few technical/product constraints and asks: 

1) Routing and control
- We need a way to pin traffic for the carveout: per-api-key routing or header-based routing is required. That’s doable but needs a small control-plane change to surface the config in the Console.

2) Model variant and fallbacks
- To hit 50ms P95 we may need to route to a distilled/quantized model variant or a GPU-resident hot pool. We must agree on quality tradeoffs and a testing plan.

3) Telemetry and SLO measurement
- We need shared telemetry definitions (what counts as P95 requests, measurement windows, and how to exclude warm-up / retries). Propose a joint eval window (2 weeks) before the SLA goes live.

4) Rollout gating
- Start with a single region (us-west) and 5% traffic, ramp to target over 7 days once metrics look good.

Action items for product:
- Draft feature-flag routing spec (Grace)
- Define measurement spec (Grace + David)
- Agree on test datasets and quality gates with Luminate

Grace
Director, Product
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Feasibility notes from infra/ops — rough, initial estimates: 

- Capacity: a dedicated hot pool sized for low-latency paths is required. For ~2M calls/day with peak windows, estimate 8-12 A100-equivalent GPU instances depending on batching efficiency.
- Cost delta: roughly 3.5x baseline cost for those routes (we can refine with profiler runs).
- Engineering ops: we’ll need a runbook (on-call escalation, automated health checks, canary rollback plan). This increases on-call load for the first 90 days of the pilot.
- Reliability tradeoff: to offer 50ms P95 we need prewarming + KV prefix caching and aggressive batching control. If traffic surges beyond expected profile, we must auto-fail to a compatible model (lower-latency but possibly lower-quality) as Grace recommended.

I can put together a more detailed cost estimate and a sample runbook (attached a draft). Questions: do we want dedicated pool in a single AZ or multi-AZ replication? Multi-AZ improves availability but doubles cost.

Attaching: luminate-runbook-draft.md, cost-estimate.xlsx

-David
Principal Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
